artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group G equipped with a lattice order ≤ such that the group multiplication is order-preserving in both arguments (equivalently, x ≤ y implies axb ≤ ayb for all a,b ∈ G). For a positive integer n, let F_n denote the free lattice-ordered group on n generators, i.e., the free object on n generators in the variety of lattice-ordered groups (with signature consisting of the group operations together with the lattice operations ∨ and ∧). Let Th(F_n) denote the first-order theory of F_n in this signature, that is, the set of all first-order sentences (in the language of ℓ-groups) that hold in F_n.

Determine, for each integer n ≥ 2, whether Th(F_n) is decidable.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results address the closely related question for free abelian ℓ-groups (where Th(FA_ℓ(n)) is decidable iff n ∈ {1,2}) and confirm that the word problem for free ℓ-groups is decidable, but no source was found settling decidability of the full first-order theory Th(F_n) of the (non-abelian) free lattice-ordered group for n ≥ 2. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Free abelian lattice-ordered groups
status_evidence.snippet: Decidability of the first-order theory of free abelian ℓ-groups depends on the number of generators (decidable only for small n).
status_evidence.claim: Related case (abelian) is settled, but addresses a different variety than free ℓ-groups.

status_evidence.title: Proof theory for lattice-ordered groups
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses proof theory and the word problem for free ℓ-groups, without resolving full first-order decidability.
status_evidence.claim: Word problem decidable; full theory not settled in this source.

status_evidence.title: Ordering groups and validity in lattice-ordered groups
status_evidence.snippet: Treats validity questions in ℓ-groups; does not establish decidability of Th(F_n) for free ℓ-groups.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of Th(F_n) decidability for n ≥ 2 found.
